page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz and includes a 25 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AVX and FMA instruction sets. The instance is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.88 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations position the c4.4xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks. The system achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 15219.95 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7354.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached rate of 851.49 GB/sec, which drops to 89.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In application-specific tests, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 11.52 GB/sec and a software compilation score of 13105.0. However, database performance is mixed; while Passmark database operations scored 5697.42, Redis SET operations registered in the lower tier at 6.16 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.4xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio designed for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs keeps the resource profile streamlined for pure processing tasks. This server is suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, batch processing, and moderate-scale machine learning inference, as evidenced by its text generation speed of 163.35 tokens per second on a small 135M model.
